rubric: A table with the options as named and 4 to 6 rows of points that matter for this user; cells short, facts and judgements kept apart.
One recommendation sentence with the condition that flips it; a tie named as a tie with a tie-breaker.
No invented prices, specifications, ratings or dates; ranges or 'usually' with a note to check.
The user's own criteria come first in the table; at most one or two added alternatives, named as added.
Uncertainty line says what to check and where.
